advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Apply the `not r.retired` exclusion consistently to the flag-derived sets (_INTERCEPTS/_HIDDEN_ALIASES/_NO_AUTO_MOUNT/_LEGACY_OUTPUT/_CONFIRM_SCOPE) in derive_policy_sets, or document why retired routes must be included there.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:208: `derived[set_name] = frozenset(r.name for r in ROUTES if r.group == group and not r.retired)`
src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:209: `derived["_INTERCEPTS"] = frozenset(r.name for r in ROUTES if r.intercept)`
src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:213: `derived["_CONFIRM_SCOPE"] = frozenset(r.name for r in ROUTES if r.confirmable)`

ABSENCE: the retired routes are excluded from group sets but not from the five flag sets; currently inert because `test_hidden_ships_but_retired_bridge_tokens_do_not` asserts no retired route ships, so no test would catch the asymmetry.
advisory.finding: derive_policy_sets() applies the `not r.retired` exclusion only to the group-derived sets in the _GROUP_TO_SET loop, but the flag-derived sets (_INTERCEPTS, _HIDDEN_ALIASES, _NO_AUTO_MOUNT, _LEGACY_OUTPUT, _CONFIRM_SCOPE) include a route regardless of its retired flag. A future retired route carrying intercept/hidden/no_auto_mount/legacy_output/confirmable would leak into those derived sets and silently break shadow parity with the router.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `and not r.retired` to each flag-derived comprehension in derive_policy_sets (e.g. `frozenset(r.name for r in ROUTES if r.intercept and not r.retired)`), mirroring the group-derived filter.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive test asserting a well-formed 'module.path:attr' reference on a non-retired route yields no malformed_reference finding, and cover the empty-module/empty-attr and non-identifier reject branches.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:220-227 `_is_valid_reference` has 4 distinct reject branches plus the accept path
tests only assert `"malformed_reference" in _codes(...)` for `handler="not-a-dotted-ref"` (line 161) and `parser_factory="bogus"` (line 165) — both trigger the `count(':') != 1` branch

ABSENCE: no `"malformed_reference" not in _codes([_route(..., handler="m:f")])` positive assertion exists; the only valid ref 'm:f' (line 170) is paired with retired=True so the assertion targets 'contradiction', not reference validity
advisory.finding: _is_valid_reference has no positive-path test: no test asserts a well-formed 'module.path:attr' handler/parser_factory reference on a non-retired route validates CLEAN (no malformed_reference finding). Both malformed tests feed inputs ('not-a-dotted-ref', 'bogus') that hit only the `ref.count(':') != 1` branch; the empty-module/empty-attr and non-identifier branches, and the accept path, are never exercised. A regression that made _is_valid_reference over-reject valid references would pass the entire suite.
scenarios: _is_valid_reference is refactored/broken to reject well-formed 'mod.sub:attr' refs
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert "malformed_reference" not in _codes([_route("x", handler="rebar._commands.transition:run")])` and parametrized malformed cases ':f', 'm:', 'm..x:f', 'm:not ident'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a derivation test with a synthetic retired route asserting it is excluded from the group-derived sets (and pin the intended behavior for the overlay sets _INTERCEPTS/_CONFIRM_SCOPE/etc).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py group-derived line uses `... if r.group == group and not r.retired`, but derived['_INTERCEPTS'] = `frozenset(r.name for r in ROUTES if r.intercept)` (and _HIDDEN_ALIASES/_NO_AUTO_MOUNT/_LEGACY_OUTPUT/_CONFIRM_SCOPE) omit the retired filter
tests/unit/test_cli_registry.py:106 `assert all(not route.retired for route in _registry.ROUTES)` — shipped table has no retired route
ABSENCE: derive_policy_sets is only ever called on the shipped ROUTES; no test passes a synthetic table containing a retired route to observe whether retired members are excluded from derived sets
advisory.finding: derive_policy_sets() applies a `not r.retired` filter to group-derived sets but NOT to the overlay sets (_INTERCEPTS, _HIDDEN_ALIASES, _NO_AUTO_MOUNT, _LEGACY_OUTPUT, _CONFIRM_SCOPE), and no test feeds a retired route through derivation. The shipped table has zero retired routes (test_hidden_ships_but_retired_bridge_tokens_do_not asserts `all(not route.retired ...)`), so the retired-exclusion contract of derive_policy_sets is entirely unverified — a retired route would still leak into every overlay set (and the retired filter for group sets is never exercised either).
scenarios: a future story adds a retired route and expects it excluded from _INTERCEPTS/_CONFIRM_SCOPE etc.
the group-set retired filter is removed in a refactor
